What is a pixel, and what does "8-bit grayscale" mean?
column2: A pixel is one sample of an image on a grid: the smallest element, with one brightness (or colour) value. 8-bit grayscale means each pixel is one number from 0 (black) to 255 (white): 2⁸ = 256 levels.

Thu 01 Oct · Baseline check (what you know today) · Q4 · Recall

What do SOC and SOH mean for a battery?
column2:
SOC (State of Charge): charge left, as a % of the cell's present full capacity, like a fuel gauge.
SOH (State of Health): present full capacity (or resistance) compared with when new. Example: 80% SOH = the cell stores only 80% of its original capacity.

Define voltage and current, with their units.
column2: Voltage: energy per unit charge between two points (1 V = 1 J/C). Current: rate of charge flow (1 A = 1 C/s). Voltage is always between two points; current flows through a point in a path.

Fri 02 Oct · Topic of Thu 01 Oct: charge, voltage, current, resistance · Q2 · Why

Why do you measure voltage in parallel but current in series?
column2:
Voltage is a difference between two points, so the probes go across them (parallel). The meter's input resistance is very high (~10 MΩ), so it barely disturbs the circuit.
Current must flow through the meter, so you break the loop and insert it (series). In current mode the meter has very low resistance: connected in parallel across a source it acts as a short circuit and can blow its fuse or damage the source.

Fri 02 Oct · Topic of Thu 01 Oct: charge, voltage, current, resistance · Q4 · Apply

An 18650 cell is labelled "3.6 V, 3000 mAh". What does each number mean for a device designer?
column2:
3.6 V is the nominal (average) voltage. The real voltage moves from about 4.2 V (full) to 2.5–3.0 V (empty), so your circuit must work across that whole range.
3000 mAh is the charge it delivers under the datasheet's test conditions (current, temperature, cut-off). Roughly 3 A for 1 h or 0.3 A for 10 h.
Energy ≈ 3.6 V × 3 Ah = 10.8 Wh.

Fri 02 Oct · Topic of Thu 01 Oct: charge, voltage, current, resistance · Q5 · Explain

Aloud, 60 s: explain voltage, current and resistance using one analogy.
column2: Model answer: "Think of water in a pipe. Voltage is the pressure difference that pushes the water. Current is how much water flows per second. Resistance is how narrow the pipe is: a narrower pipe allows less flow for the same pressure. In a circuit, the battery provides the pressure, wires are the pipes and resistors are the narrow sections."

Sat 03 Oct · Topic of Fri 02 Oct: math toolkit + Python basics · Q2 · Why

Why do engineers use percent error, and how do you calculate it?
column2:
It shows an error relative to the true value, so you can compare accuracy across different ranges.
% error = (measured − true) / true × 100.
Example: measured 4.17 V, true 4.20 V → −0.71%.

Sun 04 Oct · Topic of Sat 03 Oct: bench basics + STM32 → UART → Python · Q2 · Why

Why must you never measure resistance in a powered circuit?
column2: The ohmmeter pushes its own small current and measures the resulting voltage. An external voltage corrupts the reading and can damage the meter. Also, other parts in parallel change the reading: for accuracy, measure the resistor out of circuit (or lift one leg).

A "10 kΩ ±5%" resistor measures 9.87 kΩ. Is it within tolerance? What is the % error?
column2:
Allowed range: 9.5 – 10.5 kΩ → yes, within tolerance.
% error = (9.87 − 10) / 10 × 100 = −1.3%.

Sun 04 Oct · Topic of Sat 03 Oct: bench basics + STM32 → UART → Python · Q4 · Apply

Name three rules for handling a bare 18650 cell safely on your bench.
column2:
1. Fuse in series and a current-limited supply or proper charger.
2. Never short the terminals: cover exposed metal, keep tools and jewellery away.
3. Charge only with a Li-ion charger (CC/CV to 4.2 V), never unattended, on a non-flammable surface.
Also: don't use cells with damaged wraps; don't discharge below the datasheet minimum.

Aloud, 60 s: describe the path of data when the STM32 sends "hello" to your Python script.
column2: Model answer: "The firmware writes bytes to the STM32's UART peripheral. The UART sends them bit by bit on the TX pin at a set baud rate, for example 115200. A USB-to-serial chip, or the ST-LINK virtual COM port on a Nucleo, converts them to USB. Windows shows a COM port, and my Python script opens that port with pyserial at the same baud rate and reads the bytes."
